ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Two-thirds of the employee's average weekly wage, not more than the State average weekly wage and not less than $50 (Md. Code, Lab. & Empl. § 9-621(a)).
ttd.minText: If the employee's average weekly wage is below $50, compensation equals the actual average weekly wage (Lab. & Empl. § 9-621(a)(2)).

waiting.text: If temporary total disability lasts 14 days or less, compensation is not allowed for the first 3 calendar days (medical, hospital and funeral payments excepted); longer disability is paid from the start (Lab. & Empl. § 9-620).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid for the period that the covered employee is temporarily totally disabled; no fixed week cap (Lab. & Empl. § 9-621(b)).

ppd.text: PPD is awarded in weeks (scheduled losses such as thumb 100 weeks, index finger 40 weeks under § 9-627) at a rate that rises with the size of the award: under 75 weeks, 1/3 of AWW capped at 16.7% of SAWW ($257.00 for 2026 events); 75 to under 250 weeks, 2/3 of AWW capped at 1/3 of SAWW (§ 9-629); 250 weeks or more, weeks increased by one-third and paid at 2/3 of AWW capped at 75% of SAWW (§ 9-630).

facts.text: The 2026 maximum equals the State average weekly wage of $1,537.00 reported by the Maryland Department of Labor for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2025; the Commission rounds awards to the next highest dollar (§ 9-604).

Maryland's PPD rate depends on award length: minor awards under 75 weeks are paid at one-third of the worker's wage, but the minor category does not apply to certain public safety employees (§ 9-628).
Serious disability awards of 250 weeks or more are automatically increased by one-third of the number of weeks (§ 9-630(a)).
After 6 months of continuous TTD, the insurer must file vocational rehabilitation progress reports with the Commission, then every 120 days; late reports can draw a fine up to $500 (§ 9-675).
Temporary partial disability pays 50% of the difference between the pre-injury average weekly wage and the reduced wage-earning capacity (§ 9-615(a)).
